solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Secured by metal fasteners, as for radio transmitters

definitions.note: A's as radio operators say them, each A being Alfa

indicators.note: something secured by a pair of words is held fast inside them, so look within the phrase that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A workshop question about bolting radio transmitter casings shut with metal clips.
explanation.walkthrough: In the radio spelling alphabet A is Alfa, so the plural ALFAS is what a radio operator says for A's.
explanation.definitionFit: The NATO phonetic alphabet code word for the letter A is Alfa, so several of them are the letter A as radio operators spell it.

clue.text: University putting on big do: mega crackers with cheese

indicators.note: someone putting on a hairstyle ends up wearing it, so the letter sits within the hairdo
crackers means crazy, so the letters go wild

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
a big bushy hairdo
taken as written

explanation.surface: A university throws a big party with mega crackers served alongside cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big do' looks like a party; it is a hairdo, and U goes inside after its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Au fromage is the French menu term for a dish topped or made with cheese.

clue.text: One's firm might write angrily to me

indicators.note: writing angrily is writing in a disordered rage, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: all eighteen letters are used

explanation.surface: A complaint that one's company might send me an angry letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in my opinion, as seen from my point of view, which is what 'to me' means in 'it seems right to me'.

clue.text: Celebrated their fancy coming in, of course!

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine or embellish, so the word is rearranged
coming in means entering, so the rearranged letters go inside

blocks.note: sung of in praise
taken as written

explanation.surface: Of course they celebrated as their fancy guests arrived!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a noun, their fancy; here it rearranges THEIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure thing is an informal reply of agreement, like certainly or of course.

clue.text: Implement on table Spooner says put an end to child

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of neighbouring words, so the phrase must have its initial sounds exchanged

blocks.note: to put an end to is to stop, and a child is a chick; Spooner swaps the ST and CH sounds

explanation.surface: An odd instruction about table utensils and ending a child, attributed to Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of STOP CHICK, the ST and CH, and you get CHOP STICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A chopstick is one of a pair of eating utensils, an implement laid on the dining table.

clue.text: Town man implicated in naughty secret letters…

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters do not stay in order

blocks.note: a man is referred to as he
taken as written

explanation.surface: A local man is caught up in a scandal of naughty secret letters.
explanation.walkthrough: HE joins the thirteen letters of the phrase before they are mixed. Chester-le-Street is a town in County Durham, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester-le-Street is a market town in County Durham, England, so town names it by category.

clue.text: …giving cause for concern after dashing letter off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so these letters are muddled

blocks.note: on as in later, after: from then on
taken as written

explanation.surface: The scandal continues: someone is in trouble after firing off a hasty letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on the story of the clue above. 'Dashing' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the letters; off does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient on the danger list is critically ill, so the phrase describes a condition causing serious concern.

clue.text: Arranged for fight

blocks.note: set out or placed in order
as in a letter to, or for, someone

explanation.surface: A bout that has been arranged, set up for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief scrap or heated argument, an informal word for a fight.

clue.text: Everyone considered stripping at the end

indicators.note: stripping takes off the outer layer, so the first and last letters are removed

blocks.note: finally means at the end

explanation.surface: Everybody was thought about, though the stripping came last.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the F and Y off FINALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: In all means in total, counting everyone or everything together, which is everyone considered.

clue.text: Fund the kids' new pet?

blocks.note: first meaning: a shared pool of money
second meaning: a child's word for a kitten or cat

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like money for buying the children an animal; the question mark flags the childish pet name.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a pooled fund of cash, and also nursery talk for a cat or young kitten.

clue.text: The compilers' filling is in this paper like the most industrious of bakers?

definitions.text: like the most industrious of bakers?

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something, so the compilers' word goes inside the next piece
being in something means sitting within it, so that combined piece goes inside the paper

blocks.note: this puzzle appears in the Financial Times, abbreviated FT
what lies somewhere is located there
the setters speaking of themselves say our

explanation.surface: The setters boast that what fills this newspaper is fit for the busiest baker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' becomes lies in the sense of 'is located'. The definition is playful: a baker who works hardest gets most covered in flour.
explanation.definitionFit: Floury means covered in flour, and a hard-working baker ends up dustiest, so the superlative fits with a question mark.

clue.text: Brown, perfectly done square cuts

indicators.note: something that cuts into a thing goes inside it, so the square's letter goes into the phrase

blocks.note: done to a T means done perfectly
S as a short form of square

explanation.surface: Something browned to perfection and cut into neat squares, like a slice of toast.
explanation.walkthrough: TO A T has S slipped in after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast bread is to brown it under heat, so the verb brown is a synonym.

clue.text: "I'd better get back to work" (Yorick)

blocks.note: surface reading: anyone returning to the job after a break
setter's reading: Yorick is the dead jester in Hamlet, whose work clothes were a fool's multicoloured costume

explanation.walkthrough: Motley is the parti-coloured dress of a court jester, and the phrase, from the opera Pagliacci, means the show must go on.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock phrase is a performer's call to dress up and carry on, which is a jester like Yorick getting back to his trade.

clue.text: Studio theatre off-Broadway rejects article containing fabrication

indicators.note: what a word rejects it throws out, so the article is dropped from the theatre word
containing means holding something inside, so the fabrication goes within what remains

blocks.note: off-Broadway is in America, where the word is spelt with ER
the definite article
a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: A small New York theatre turns down an article that contains a made-up story.
explanation.walkthrough: Off-Broadway signals the American spelling, ending ER. The fabrication goes in just before the final letter of what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's workshop, which is what a studio is.

clue.text: Greatly distress adult very loudly getting battered on the ear

indicators.note: something heard on the ear is judged by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
fortissimo, marked ff in music
licked means beaten soundly

explanation.surface: A grown-up, hit hard and yelling, is clearly in great distress.
explanation.walkthrough: In music ff means very loud.
explanation.definitionFit: To afflict someone is to cause them suffering or great trouble, a verb matching greatly distress.

clue.text: Poor rector evicted by estate agent?

indicators.note: someone evicted by a landlord is put out, so the abbreviation goes out of the following phrase

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for rector
the question mark allows a playful description of one who deals in flats

explanation.surface: A poor vicar thrown out of his home by an estate agent.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate agent is the British term for a realtor, here imagined as a broker of flats.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat broke is an informal phrase for having no money at all, completely poor.

clue.text: See 2
They managed monster's home in absence of male dictator

indicators.note: in the absence of something means without it, so the male pronoun is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
the male pronoun
ran a business means managed it
Loch Ness, Scottish lake said to house the monster

explanation.surface: People ran a monster's lair without any men, under a dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove HE from THEY to get TY. Fittingly, the male is taken out of a word for a female ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyranness is a female tyrant, an oppressive absolute ruler, which is a dictator.

clue.text: Back fresh cycling class for Games centrepiece

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round from one end to the other like a wheel turning
back means going in the opposite direction, so the whole string is read from its end

blocks.note: green means new or inexperienced
physical education, the school lesson for sports

explanation.surface: A school sports lesson returning to support a centrepiece at the Games.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotate GREEN to ENGRE by moving letters from front to back, add PE, then read ENGREPE backwards. In British schools Games is the sports lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is an ornamental branched stand placed in the middle of a dining table, a table centrepiece.

clue.text: Does one sing part of retiring songstress? Arguably

definitions.note: a question form: a grasser is one who sings to the police

indicators.note: part of a phrase is a run of letters inside it
retiring means going back, so the hidden letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: the run spans the tail of the first word and the head of the second

explanation.surface: Does a shy female singer really sing, one might argue?
explanation.walkthrough: To sing in slang is to inform on others, and grass is slang for an informer; 'sing' looks musical next to songstress.
explanation.definitionFit: A grasser is a slang informer, someone who sings, that is, tells the police what they know.

clue.text: The stick one takes for the players' performance

definitions.text: The stick one takes for the players' performance

blocks.note: surface reading: punishment or blame accepted on behalf of a team
setter's reading: the players are an orchestra, and the stick is the one waved in front of them

explanation.walkthrough: Taking stick means suffering criticism, so it sounds like a manager blamed for a bad team display; the players are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin rod held by the person leading an orchestra is the stick used to direct the musicians' performance.

clue.text: Hear Catholic worshipping?

blocks.note: C is an abbreviation for Catholic
worshipping means at church, abbreviated CH

explanation.surface: A question about hearing Catholics at their worship.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the cryptic step from worshipping to being at church.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch what someone says is to hear it, as in 'I didn't catch that'.

clue.text: The number in this group rising would make 19?

blocks.note: surface reading: a headcount of some unnamed group, and the group has nine members
setter's reading: read upwards in the down grid the answer says ten on, and nine plus ten on makes nineteen

explanation.walkthrough: The 19 looks like a cross-reference to the clue numbered 19; it is the plain number nineteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine musicians or a piece for nine, so its number is nine.

clue.text: Rust coloured, one's dresses

indicators.note: what dresses something clothes it, so the answer is wrapped inside the words

blocks.note: the run spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone's dresses are coloured a rusty shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Uredo is a stage of rust fungus on plants, a botanical word for the disease called rust.

clue.text: Nail-biting time

blocks.note: first meaning: anxious and suspenseful
second meaning: the grammatical form of a verb showing when

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about a nervous moment; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense is both an adjective for strained suspense and the grammar term for a verb form marking past, present or future.

clue.text: Typify US songwriters Paul and Michael, poles apart, returning home at last

indicators.note: the two compass poles are split off and sent away from the middle of the joined names
returning means going back the way it came, so the remaining string is read backwards
at last points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: Paul Simon, American singer-songwriter
Michael Stipe, singer and lyricist of REM
north and south
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Two American songwriters typify being far apart yet coming home in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: SIMONSTIPE has N and S side by side in the middle; remove them, reverse SIMOTIPE, then add E.
explanation.definitionFit: To epitomise something is to be a perfect example of it, which is what typify means.

clue.text: Fly returned money to Bristol Hospital nurses

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the money word and the one after it are read backwards
to nurse is to hold close, so these letters cradle the reversed piece

blocks.note: oof is old slang for cash
taken as written
H is the map abbreviation for hospital
rhyming slang: Bristol City means titty, a breast

explanation.surface: Money returned to a Bristol hospital where nurses work, one quick flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Bristols is British rhyming slang for breasts, from Bristol City. Bristol looks like the city, but it gives a breast, and the hospital's H sits before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hotfoot it is to hurry off, and fly is a casual verb for leaving in a rush.

clue.text: Golf club with missing 6-9 inches

indicators.note: missing means left out, so the abbreviation for with is removed from the club

blocks.note: a wedge is a lofted iron
W is short for with
six minus nine in Roman numerals, IX, leaves just S

explanation.surface: A golf club with a missing section of six to nine inches.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash is a minus sign: SIX take away IX leaves S. Inches looks like a measurement; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge forward is to move slowly, a little at a time, which is the verb inches.
